overall: AG declined the Aug 7 and Sept 18 executive session claims as untimely. For Dec 4, 2023, it found a proper executive session purpose, adequate notice, and timely minutes review, with no duty to read aloud absent a request. No violation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Aug 7 and Sept 18, 2023 executive sessions lacked a proper purpose; the complaint was filed in May 2024, months after both meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Where the complaint regarding the August 7 and September 18 meetings was not filed until May 3, 2024, we find that it was untimely and we decline to review the allegations.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the Dec 4, 2023 executive session had no lawful identified purpose under the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: After review, we find that the Council permissibly convened in executive session on December 4.

allegations.summary: The Dec 4, 2023 notice topic was to approve the minutes of the Aug 7 and Sept 18 executive sessions; the letter assessed whether that topic was sufficiently specific.
First complaint alleged the Council failed to review and release the minutes of the Dec 4, 2023 executive session.
allegations.key_passage: We find that this review, exactly six months after the meeting in question, satisfied the Council's obligations under the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Second complaint alleged that when the Council approved the Dec 4 minutes for release on June 3, 2024, it did not read them aloud or distribute them.
allegations.key_passage: Furthermore, in the absence of any request for the minutes, the Council was not required to read aloud or otherwise distribute the December 4 executive session minutes.
